description: Composite EBSD figure (Inverse Pole Figure and Pole Figure maps) of low-density Fe-28Mn-8Al-1C steel at three deformation degrees. (a) is an IPF orientation map of the undeformed condition, 50 µm scale bar, showing equiaxed austenite grains in random rainbow colours bounded by thin and thick black boundary lines, with insets of the IPF colour triangle and two cubic unit-cell sketches. (b) is the CR 30% IPF map, 20 µm scale bar, with colour triangle inset; grains remain roughly equiaxed but subdivide into colour-banded subgrains. (c) is the CR 90% IPF map, 5 µm scale bar; the original grains are completely fragmented into fine RD-elongated rolling bands, bright banded colours alternating with dark, largely unindexed stringers. Interleaved with the maps are three sets of {100}, {110} and {111} circular pole figures, plotted with RD vertical and TD horizontal and a blue (low) to red (high) contour colour scale. The undeformed set is weak and nearly uniform; the CR 30% set develops discrete red maxima; the CR 90% set shows a strong central maximum in the {110} figure, consistent with a brass-type texture. No numerical texture or misorientation values are printed on any panel.

subfigures.description: EBSD inverse pole figure (IPF) orientation map of the undeformed test steel with a 50 µm scale bar; large equiaxed grains with random (rainbow) orientations separated by thin and thick black boundary lines. Insets: IPF colour triangle (bottom right) and two cube unit-cell schematic sketches (right).

IPF orientation map after CR 30% with a 20 µm scale bar and IPF colour triangle inset; grains are still roughly equiaxed but subdivided into colour-banded subgrains with numerous black boundary lines.

IPF orientation map after CR 90% with a 5 µm scale bar and IPF colour triangle inset; the microstructure is a banded, fibrous structure of austenite grains elongated along RD, with bright banded colour regions alternating with dark, largely unindexed bands (rolling bands).

Three circular {100}, {110} and {111} pole figures with RD vertical and TD horizontal; intensity contours are weak and near-uniformly distributed with only isolated yellow/red maxima, i.e. little texture.

Three circular {100}, {110} and {111} pole figures with RD/TD cross lines; the intensity distribution resolves into several strong, discrete red maxima, indicating texture development after 30% cryogenic rolling.

Three circular {100}, {110} and {111} pole figures; the {110} figure shows a pronounced maximum near its centre and the {100}/{111} figures show split elongated maxima, consistent with a brass-type texture after 90% cryogenic rolling.

observations.observation: The figure combines three EBSD inverse pole figure orientation maps with three matching sets of {100}, {110} and {111} pole figures; it is therefore a composite EBSD texture figure.
Panel (a) carries a 50 µm scale bar; the undeformed structure consists of large equiaxed grains coloured across the full IPF colour wheel, i.e. without a dominant orientation.
Panel (b) carries a 20 µm scale bar and shows the CR 30% condition, with grains still roughly equiaxed but subdivided by numerous internal boundary lines into colour-banded subgrains.

Panel (c) carries a 5 µm scale bar and shows the CR 90% condition, where the equiaxed grains are replaced by banded, RD-elongated fibrous structures with dark, low-indexed bands interpreted as rolling bands.
The pole figures are plotted as circular maps with RD vertical and TD horizontal; intensity is encoded as a blue-to-red contour scale with no numeric intensity legend printed.

Across the three pole figure sets the contour pattern changes from weak, nearly uniform intensity (undeformed) to discrete strong maxima (CR 30%) to a pronounced central {110} maximum with split {100}/{111} maxima (CR 90%).
The caption states that the panels correspond to test steel at different deformation degrees: a) undeformed, b) CR 30%, and c) CR 90%.
The caption describes the figure as inverse pole figure and pole figure maps; it does not mention any KAM map, although the citing text refers to KAM maps in other figures.
The citing text states that the undeformed equiaxed austenite grains have relatively random orientations with 94.65% high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs).
The citing text states that a sharp misorientation peak at 60° corresponds to twin boundaries 60<111> in Figure 5a; no misorientation-angle axis or peak is visible in this figure group.
The citing text states that after 30% CR the copper {112}<111> texture component appears and the proportion of low-angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) rises to 89.4%.

The citing text states that at CR 90% the initial equiaxed grains are completely fragmented into banded austenite structures elongated along RD, LAGBs reach 94.1%, and the copper component changes to the brass {110}<112> component.
The citing text attributes higher KAM values near prior grain boundaries at CR 30% and in the rolling bands at CR 90%; the panels supplied here contain no KAM colour scale to confirm this.
